chunks: He said: Abu Bakr Muhammad ibn Umar al-Ji'abi informed me, saying: Abu al-Husayn al-Abbas ibn al-Mughirah narrated to us, saying: Abu Bakr Ahmad ibn Mansur al-Ramadi narrated to us, saying: Sulayman ibn Harb narrated to us, saying: Hammad ibn Zayd narrated to us, from Yahya ibn Sa'id, from Asim ibn Ubayd Allah, from Abd al-Rahman ibn Aban ibn Uthman, from his father, from Uthman ibn Affan, who said:

I was the last of the people to have seen Umar ibn al-Khattab. I entered upon him while his head was in the lap of his son Abdullah, and he was despondent. He said to him: "Put my cheek on the ground." But Abdullah refused. He then said: "Put my cheek on the ground, may your mother be bereaved of you!" So he placed his cheek on the ground. He kept saying: "Woe to my mother! Woe to my mother, if You do not forgive me!" He continued to say this until his soul departed.

key_terms.لا أم لك: May your mother be bereaved of you — a strong Arabic expression of rebuke urging compliance
key_terms.ملول: Despondent, weary, distressed — describing Umar's state on his deathbed
key_terms.ويل أمي: Woe to my mother — an Arabic expression of distress and self-lament

ai.seo_question: What were the last words of Umar ibn al-Khattab before his death?
ai.summary: This hadith records the final moments of Umar ibn al-Khattab, the second caliph, as witnessed by Uthman ibn Affan. On his deathbed after being stabbed by Abu Lu'lu'a in 23 AH, Umar insisted that his son Abdullah place his cheek on the ground as an act of humility before God. His dying words were a plea for divine forgiveness, reflecting his fear of the reckoning despite his high status in the early Muslim community.
